answer: A working Sybil defense is a per-agent bond slashed on identity reuse. An agent locks a stake before submitting work, and identities link through attestations co-signed when they transact or grade each other. Those links act like a pearl in that each new identity adds a visible layer, so accounts run by one operator form a dense cluster, and the cluster loses its bond, not one seat. A farmer pays the stake per fake identity and risks one slashing wiping all of them, so cost climbs while payout stays flat. The bond is as costly per unit as saffron and reveals shared owners like an opal does.
